items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: the gentleman that took Davy Tough’s place in the Woody Herman band with my father, his name is Don Lamond... he definitely taught me a lot about just the technique of the drumset.

ctx.x: Yeah. Didn’t you learn from a tap dancer?
Most definitely. Steve Condos, who is part of the famous Condos Brothers dance team. When I was four years old, my dad taught me pulse and groove from a bass player, and © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

then I learned rhythms and accents from a tap dancer. So that’s a unique way to approach the drums. And the gentleman that took Davy Tough’s place in the Woody Herman band with my father, his name is Don Lamond, he’s still with us, very healthy and happy in Orlando, Florida, and still playing great, and he definitely taught me a lot about just the technique of the drumset.
